title: Why Agent Hype can fall short of reality – Joel Becker, METR
talk_summary: METR contrasts benchmark-style evidence (time-horizon doubling ~every 6-7 months) with a field RCT where 16 expert developers on large mature repos were 19% slower with AI allowed, despite predicting 24% speedup and reporting 20% speedup afterward. The reconciliation hinges on reliability thresholds, low-context vs high-context baselines, messy real tasks, and task interdependence.

takeaways.technique: Reliability threshold for trusting agent output
takeaways.what_they_do: Argue that AI must be correct ~95-99% of the time before humans can 'tab through' without costly verification; below that, checking/correcting work erases gains.
takeaways.numbers: 95-99% reliability needed to save time; observed 19% slowdown

takeaways.what_they_do: Randomly assign real work items to AI-allowed vs AI-disallowed and measure actual completion time, rather than trusting benchmark scores or self-reported speedup.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we find that developers are slowed down by 19%. They take 19% more time when AI is allowed

takeaways.what_they_do: Note that benchmark humans are low-context 'first week on the job'; experts who already know the solution are limited by typing speed, so delegating to AI adds instruction overhead.
Observe that if a human must know how subtask A was done to do subtask B, delegating A to AI loses context and can be net negative even if AI is faster at A.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they need to know how how task A was completed in order to reliably complete task B

takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguish costless algorithmic scoring (unit tests) from holistic 'mergeability' scoring that accounts for maintainability and quality not captured by tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sweet scores are not trying to account for ... whether the code is spilled honable by by other people in future

takeaways.what_they_do: Warn that agentic benchmarks use small contained environments without human coordination, unlike real large repos, so benchmark success overstates real-world performance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the problems aren't very messy ... not these sort of massive open source code bases
